exceptions.reason: The button writes `data-orientation`. It writes no `data-disabled`: CSS selects `:disabled` and `[aria-disabled='true']` (rule 8.15). It writes no `data-focusable`, which repeats the prop `focusableWhenDisabled`; the state keeps `focusable`. The family has no namespace of constants (rule 8.10).
The group writes the attribute names that the docs list, and CSS selects them as text. The family has no namespace of constants (rule 8.10).

The input writes `data-orientation`. It writes no `data-disabled`: CSS selects `:disabled` and `[aria-disabled='true']` (rule 8.15). It writes no `data-focusable`, which repeats the prop `focusableWhenDisabled`; the state keeps `focusable`. The family has no namespace of constants (rule 8.10).
The link writes `data-orientation`, and CSS selects it as text. The family has no namespace of constants (rule 8.10).

The root writes `aria-orientation`, which the role `toolbar` takes, so CSS selects `[aria-orientation='vertical']`, and it writes no `data-orientation` (rule 8.15). It writes `data-disabled`. The family has no namespace of constants (rule 8.10).

The part writes `aria-orientation`, which the role `separator` takes, so CSS selects `[aria-orientation='vertical']` and the part writes no `data-orientation` (rule 8.15). The family has no namespace of constants (rule 8.10).

`Toolbar.test.ts` tests that the keys move the focus over a disabled input, which keeps no key, in each orientation.

`Toolbar.compose.test.ts` renders `NumberField.Input` in the `element` slot of `Toolbar.Input`: the keys of the axis move the focus, the other keys step it, and a disabled input keeps the focus and does not step.

`Toolbar.test.ts` tests the `<a>` element with its attributes, `data-orientation`, and a link that stays enabled in a disabled toolbar.

surfaceAdditions.reason: `Toolbar.Input` gives `v-model` to the `Input` that it renders (rule 8.5).
`Toolbar.Input` gives `id` to the `Input` that it renders, or to the element of its `element` slot. The `id` names the element that takes the focus (rule 8.4).
`Toolbar.Input` gives `name` to the `Input` that it renders, or to the element of its `element` slot, for the form data.
`Toolbar.Input` adds `readonly` to the read-only state of a disabled input that keeps the focus, so the part declares it.
`Toolbar.Input` gives the change event of the `Input` that it renders, with its details (rule 8.6).
`Toolbar.Input` gives the model update of the `Input` that it renders, for `v-model` (rule 8.5).

relocations.behavior: The button is an item of the toolbar, by the button rule of the library.
The group adds its disabled state to the toolbar of the items in it.
The input is an item of the toolbar, and a disabled input that keeps the focus is read-only.
The link is an item of the toolbar that is never disabled.
The types of the native attributes of a link, and of the parts.
The root lists the items, gives the tab stop, moves the focus with the arrow keys, and stops the presses and the keys of a disabled item.
The separator is across the toolbar.
